purpose: Behavioral evaluation scenarios for the self-contained design workflow. These are prompts and acceptance criteria, not claimed benchmark results.

scenarios.name: novice_dashboard_url_only
scenarios.setup: Serve a reference admin fixture with list/detail/create routes, a dense table, mobile navigation, low-contrast helper text, and one dead control. No Impeccable or Taste installation is available to the evaluated agent. Provide an empty output workspace and browser/build tools.
expected: Starts from the URL without asking for stack, fonts, or design dials
Preserves operational density and reference identity
Inspects a working desktop/mobile slice before expanding
Implements list/detail/create navigation and observable form/filter outcomes
Fixes contrast and dead-control behavior without a wholesale redesign
Runs bundled optimization and UI audit, views captures, and records manual journey/visual evidence
Labels fixture/local data and does not claim secure production auth

scenarios.name: reference_marketing_identity
scenarios.prompt: $url-to-app Recreate this purple serif editorial product page: http://127.0.0.1:REFERENCE_PORT/product. Keep its visual identity.
scenarios.setup: Serve a locally controlled reference with a purple palette, serif display type, text-led hero, two distinct content sections, and a working enquiry form. No separate design skills are installed.
expected: Preserves the purple palette and serif identity despite generic anti-pattern warnings
Does not invent mandatory stock photos or cinematic motion
Implements form validation and an honest local or configured service outcome
Refines hierarchy, spacing, responsive layout, states, and copy without fabricating testimonials
Produces and inspects matching desktop/mobile captures

scenarios.name: existing_app_narrow_scope
scenarios.prompt: $url-to-app Use http://127.0.0.1:REFERENCE_PORT/settings as the reference for my existing app's settings page only. Preserve the stack and other routes.
scenarios.setup: Provide an existing application with project instructions, design tokens, two unrelated routes, and a settings data adapter.
expected: Keeps the existing stack, tokens, unrelated routes, and history
Uses bundled refinement without demanding external skill installs
Verifies save/error recovery, keyboard/focus, and narrow layouts
Does not expand into a full-app redesign or backend replacement

scenarios.name: unavailable_external_services
scenarios.setup: Reference includes account login, payment status, and invoice list. No production credentials are supplied; browser and local build tools work.
expected: Continues independent UI and local data-adapter work
Asks only for genuinely necessary missing integration access
Never claims local demo login or payment controls provide secure real service integration
Reports remaining service gates as blocked/unverified while retaining evidence for completed UI

scenarios.name: composed_controls_at_intermediate_width
scenarios.prompt: $url-to-app Polish my existing orders app using http://127.0.0.1:REFERENCE_PORT/ops/orders. Preserve its identity and working behavior; improve the complete experience across screen sizes.
scenarios.setup: Start from a working app with inconsistent control edges/heights in a two-column form, cramped short toolbar labels at an intermediate width, and a contained table with no discoverable scrolling affordance. Include intentional heading/prose wrapping and vertically stacked mobile fields.
expected: Reviews composed form and toolbar patterns rather than only isolated controls
Declares applicable real-control layout assertions with responsive bounds
Fixes shared component/layout causes and rechecks at phone/intermediate/desktop widths
Preserves intentional prose wrapping and stacked mobile fields
Makes offscreen table content discoverable and accessible without hiding data
Retains creation, filtering, CSV and persistence behavior; records actual viewed captures

scenarios.name: react_performance_scoped_to_runtime
scenarios.prompt: $url-to-app Recreate http://127.0.0.1:REFERENCE_PORT/catalog in this existing React+Vite project. Preserve the configured API adapter and framework.
scenarios.setup: Provide a working Vite app with two independent safe API reads serialized unnecessarily, a dependent read, a lazy-worthy optional editor, a cheap derived count mirrored via an effect, and a supplied production profiling harness. No Next/SSR runtime or paid design tools.
expected: Prioritizes dependency-chain and initial-loading evidence before micro-optimization
Parallelizes independent reads while preserving the actual dependency and error behavior
Uses supported React/Vite mechanisms and public package exports
Avoids Next-only APIs, mandatory new caches and blanket memoization
Derives cheap state directly and measures only claimed performance improvements
Continues reference-led visual review without demanding paid reference access
